statement: Every export from .eb to a legacy format produces exactly one of three outcomes: LOSSLESS, LOSSY (declared), or REFUSED, and the tool always states which outcome occurred.
research_needed: Conformance corpus test that every export path (every target format and dialect) emits exactly one outcome in both CLI output and receipt.

statement: LOSSLESS is defined as the target representing every entry, every byte, and every metadata item of the archive.
research_needed: Per-target-format capability matrix (zip, tar/pax, tar/gnu, tar.zst, 7z...) against EAM metadata classes to decide when LOSSLESS is achievable; check whether signatures, provenance and non-identity metadata count as 'metadata items'.
decision_needed: Does LOSSLESS require preserving non-identity metadata, signatures, embedded provenance and physical structure, or only LAI-bound content and captured metadata?

statement: LOSSY (declared) export: every loss must be enumerated before any output is written, and the user must accept it with --accept-loss; otherwise the export is refused.
research_needed: Verify that loss enumeration can be computed fully before writing for streamed/huge archives (bounded memory), and that no loss is discovered only mid-write.

statement: REFUSED export outcome applies when the target cannot represent the archive safely or cannot represent it at all.
research_needed: Enumerate refusal conditions per target format in a conformance matrix.

statement: Nothing is ever silently discarded during export; this is the export half of governing philosophy statement (5), 'loss is declared, never silent'.
refines_or_supersedes: Implements export half of SPEC §2.1 L94-95 philosophy statement (5); pairs with §10.9 Fidelity Report (L1309+)
research_needed: Differential tests: export then re-import and compare against receipt-declared losses to prove no undeclared loss.

statement: Exporting content-shared entries to a target that represents them as N full copies, or as link records with different semantics, is classified LOSSY.
research_needed: Map EAM content sharing to tar hardlinks, zip (no links), 7z; document semantic differences of hardlink records on extraction.
decision_needed: For targets with hardlink records, does export emit links (different semantics) or full copies by default?

statement: Exporting POSIX ACLs or xattrs to ZIP, which has no standardised representation for them, is classified LOSSY.
research_needed: Survey de facto ZIP extra fields (Info-ZIP Unix extras, macOS/Apple, libarchive) and extractor support to confirm no standard representation.
decision_needed: Should export ever write non-standard ZIP extra fields for xattrs/ACLs, or always declare the loss?

statement: Exporting nanosecond timestamps into the DOS ZIP timestamp field with two-second granularity is classified LOSSY.
research_needed: Check whether extended timestamp (0x5455) or NTFS (0x000a) ZIP extra fields reduce the loss and which extractors honour them.
decision_needed: Does ZIP export write extended/NTFS timestamp extra fields, and does that change the loss declaration?

statement: Exporting a Windows security descriptor to tar is classified LOSSY.
research_needed: Check pax extended-header conventions (e.g., libarchive/star keys) for NT security descriptors and runtime support.

statement: Exporting per-entry codec choices into a whole-archive-compressed tarball is classified LOSSY.

Per-entry codec choice is a physical, non-LAI property, yet its loss is listed as LOSSY; unclear whether physical-layout losses (codecs, random access, chunk groups) require --accept-loss, given LOSSLESS is defined over entries, bytes and metadata.
research_needed: Usability check: would requiring --accept-loss for every tar.zst export (physical-only loss) make dual publishing noisy?
decision_needed: Do physical-only differences count as LOSSY (requiring --accept-loss), or are they compatibility_notes only?

statement: Export is REFUSED when an archive containing case-colliding paths is exported to a case-insensitive target where the export would silently merge two entries.
research_needed: Real-world frequency of case-colliding paths in published trees (e.g., Linux kernel source) to size the impact on dual publishing.

statement: ZIP and tar store names as case-sensitive byte strings; 'case-insensitive target' and 'target that cannot express' reserved names are undefined: format property, target profile, or intended extraction runtime/filesystem? Also unclear whether a rename policy could downgrade REFUSED to LOSSY.
research_needed: Define export target profiles (format + intended runtime) and test which extractors merge or reject colliding/reserved names.
decision_needed: Is refusal keyed to format, to a declared target runtime profile, or both; and is a rename/mangle option permitted for export?

statement: Export is REFUSED for entries whose names are Windows-reserved when the target cannot express them.

Exporting an encrypted .eb to a format whose only encryption is unauthenticated is REFUSED unless --downgrade-encryption is given; silently converting authenticated to unauthenticated encryption is a security regression the tool will not perform quietly.
research_needed: Classify target formats' encryption (ZipCrypto, WinZip AE-1/AE-2, 7z AES-CBC, none) as authenticated or not; security review of downgrade acknowledgement UX.

statement: Unaddressed: exporting an encrypted .eb to a target with no encryption at all (plaintext tar/zip), and which outcome class (LOSSY? LOSSLESS?) and receipt record apply once --downgrade-encryption is acknowledged.
research_needed: Threat-model review of decrypt-and-export paths; compare with how age/gpg tools warn on plaintext output.
decision_needed: Is plaintext export from an encrypted archive refused without acknowledgement, and is the downgrade recorded as a declared loss in the receipt?

statement: The --downgrade-encryption acknowledgement flag required by §15.2 does not appear in the convert/export CLI synopsis in §17.5.
decision_needed: Add --downgrade-encryption to the convert/export synopsis, or rename/merge it with another acknowledgement flag?

statement: Exporting a chunk-group-dependent archive to a format with no equivalent, where the result would be correct but pathologically slow to read, is REFUSED with an explanation and a suggestion to repack first.

The chunk-group refusal case is a correctly representable result, contradicting the REFUSED definition (cannot represent safely or at all); also unclear why a legacy output's read speed depends on source chunk groups rather than target encoding, and which targets trigger it.
research_needed: Identify concrete target formats (e.g., solid 7z blocks) where source chunk-group structure would be carried into the export; measure read cost.
decision_needed: Should the performance case be REFUSED, LOSSY with a warning, or handled automatically by re-planning during export?

statement: Dual publishing (pack .eb with dense profile, then deterministic export to zip and tar.zst) is designated the primary Stage-3 adoption workflow.
research_needed: Adoption research: do release engineers accept a three-artifact pipeline; compare with existing reproducible-release tooling.

statement: All dual-published artifacts derive from one semantic source; the .eb carries the LAI and each export carries its own digests plus, in its receipt, the LAI it was derived from.

A consumer holding the .eb can verify that a given .zip was produced from it; the verification mechanism (signed receipt, deterministic re-export and byte comparison, or logical diff) is not specified, and unsigned external receipts are forgeable.
research_needed: Specify and test a derivation-verification algorithm; measure deterministic export reproducibility across platforms, tool versions and codec library versions; security review of receipt forgery.
decision_needed: How is 'produced from' verified: re-export and byte compare, logical comparison of the zip against the LAI, or a signed receipt?

statement: Claims the supply-chain property of verifying one published artifact was derived from another does not currently exist for any pair of published artifacts.
research_needed: Survey in-toto/SLSA attestations, Sigstore bundles, Reproducible Builds (buildinfo, diffoscope), npm/PyPI provenance to test the claim.

statement: Deterministic export is normative: export --deterministic yields byte-identical legacy artifacts from the same source by applying per-target normalisation rules: entry ordering, timestamp handling, header field suppression, codec parameter pinning.
research_needed: Build reproducibility test harness across OS, CPU, thread counts; verify DEFLATE/zstd encoder output stability across library versions.

statement: Scope of byte-identical deterministic export is unstated: same tool version only, or across tool versions, codec library versions, platforms and thread counts? Codec encoders (DEFLATE, zstd) do not guarantee identical output across versions.
research_needed: Measure output stability of candidate DEFLATE/zstd/xz encoders across versions; decide whether to vendor/pin encoders.
decision_needed: Is deterministic export guaranteed only within a pinned tool+encoder version, and is that version recorded in the receipt?

statement: The 'known normalisation rules for each target format' are not enumerated or versioned in this section; no normative rule set per target (zip, tar/pax, tar.zst) is given.
research_needed: Compare with Reproducible Builds archive normalisation practice (sorted order, fixed mtime, owner 0, pax header suppression) and existing tools' deterministic modes.
decision_needed: Where are per-target normalisation rules specified and how is a rule-set version identified?

statement: Worked examples use 'export <eb> --to zip --out <file>', but the convert synopsis takes a positional <dest> and defines no --out flag; CLI surface for export is inconsistent.
decision_needed: Is the output a positional argument, --out, or both for convert/export?

statement: For existing legacy artifacts that cannot be replaced, Entrybound offers a sidecar describing the artifact in Entrybound terms: entry set, digests, LAI, conversion receipt and fidelity report, without its content.
A sidecar is an ordinary .eb archive with role = Sidecar whose entries carry external content references instead of chunk references; no new extension, format or parser.
refines_or_supersedes: Consistent with §8.5 L958-965 ArchiveRole and §18.1 single extension L2025-2027

statement: 'entrybound verify release.zip --sidecar release.zip.eb' checks a legacy artifact against its sidecar description.
research_needed: Define what is checked (byte digest of whole artifact, per-entry digests via import, metadata) and under which import mode.

statement: verify synopsis accepts only <archive.eb> and lists no --sidecar or --parity options, yet other sections run verify on legacy files (release.zip --sidecar, suspicious.zip --canonical) and with --parity; what verify means for non-.eb inputs is undefined.
decision_needed: Does verify accept legacy inputs, and what does --canonical mean for a ZIP (e.g., strict-import ambiguity check)?

statement: The sidecar naming convention '<artifact>.eb' (release.zip.eb) appears only in an example; whether it is normative for discovery is unstated.
decision_needed: Is '<artifact>.eb' the normative sidecar name for automatic discovery, or is --sidecar always explicit?

statement: A sidecar carries describes_lai, the LAI of the artifact it describes, as a claim in its conversion record.
A sidecar's own LAI differs from the described LAI because it is computed over its own external-referencing entry set with role = Sidecar bound in; the two identities are never conflated.
research_needed: Formal/property test: LAI(Sidecar of X) != LAI(X) for all X; include role in canonical LAI encoding test vectors.

statement: Binding role into LAI prevents a signed Complete archive from being stripped of its content and still verifying as a valid signed archive.
research_needed: External security review / formal model of signature binding over LAI with role; attack test converting Complete to Sidecar/Incremental.

statement: What 'the LAI of' a legacy artifact is remains ambiguous: it depends on import mode (strict, compat:<runtime>, preserve) and identity profile; also whether verify --sidecar checks describes_lai or treats it as an unverified claim.
research_needed: Test whether strict vs compat imports of the same ZIP yield different LAIs on a corpus of ambiguous ZIPs.
decision_needed: Which import mode and identity profile define describes_lai, and is it recorded alongside the claim?

statement: ContentRef is a two-variant sum: Internal { content_object_id } or External { digest, length, optional locator }.
research_needed: Canonical encoding test vectors for both variants; decide digest algorithm agility for External.digest.

statement: External.locator is optional but its syntax (URL, relative path), whether it participates in LAI, and the security policy for resolving it (remote fetch, path traversal, confinement) are unspecified here.
research_needed: Security review of locator resolution; check whether changing a mirror URL should change identity.
decision_needed: Is the locator excluded from LAI, and may readers dereference remote locators automatically?

statement: Claims the External ContentRef variant is a small, well-contained addition that serves three purposes: sidecars, incremental archives referencing a base, and Stage-2 adoption computing Entrybound identities for artifacts still published as ZIP.
research_needed: Design review of External refs across verify, unpack, list, diff, salvage, export and budget declaration to confirm containment.

statement: Behaviour of unpack, list, diff, export and salvage on a role = Sidecar (content-less) archive, or on External refs generally, is not specified in this section.
decision_needed: Do content-consuming commands refuse Sidecar archives, or resolve External refs via locator/base?

statement: Stage-2 adoption: a project can compute Entrybound identities for artifacts it continues to publish as ZIP, via sidecars with External references.
research_needed: Adoption study: would projects publish sidecars alongside existing ZIPs?

statement: Every import and every export produces a ConversionRecord: a typed, machine-readable, human-printable object.
research_needed: Conformance tests that every conversion path emits a schema-valid record.

statement: ConversionRecord serialisation, canonical encoding, schema definition and schema versioning are not specified in this section (only field tables).
decision_needed: Is the ConversionRecord canonically encoded like the manifest, and how are new fields added without breaking readers?

statement: Import record field source.format records the source format and detected dialect (e.g., zip, tar/pax, tar/gnu).
research_needed: Measure dialect-detection accuracy on a corpus of tar/zip variants.

statement: Import record fields source.digest (digest of the exact source bytes) and source.size (byte length).
research_needed: Specify digest algorithm; confirm hashing while streaming from a pipe is feasible.
decision_needed: Which digest algorithm(s) does source.digest use, and is it agile?

statement: Import record field import.mode takes one of strict, compat:<runtime>, or preserve.

import.mode is single-valued, yet --compat (resolution policy) and --preserve (retaining non-semantic peculiarities) address different axes; whether they can combine, and how the record expresses a combination, is unclear.
decision_needed: Are --compat <runtime> and --preserve mutually exclusive, and if not how is import.mode encoded?

statement: Import record field import.tool records the tool and its version.
Import record field ambiguities records every conflict: subject, field, all observations with byte offsets and authorities, and the resolution applied.
refines_or_supersedes: Records resolutions of import observations defined in SPEC §14 (per §2.1 L84)
research_needed: Measure record size on adversarial inputs with very many conflicts.

statement: Enumerating every conflict, normalisation and non-semantic datum makes ConversionRecord size unbounded on adversarial legacy inputs; no size limit, truncation rule or interaction with declared resource budgets is stated.
research_needed: Fuzz/adversarial ZIP/tar inputs to measure receipt growth; check budget declarations cover CONVERSION_RECORD.
decision_needed: Is there a bound or summarisation rule for receipts, and does exceeding it refuse the import?

statement: Import record field normalisations lists every metadata transformation with before and after values.
Import record field unsupported lists source features with no native mapping and their disposition.
Import record fields discarded | preserved give an explicit disposition for every non-semantic legacy datum.
Import record fields result.lai (resulting logical archive identity) and result.identity_profile (the profile the LAI is under).
Export record fields target.format (target format and dialect) and outcome (lossless | lossy | refused).
Export record fields semantic_losses (structure that could not be represented) and metadata_losses (per metadata class, per-entry count).
§15.1 requires every loss enumerated, but metadata_losses records counts per class and entry; unclear whether the receipt must enumerate each lost item per entry or only aggregate counts.
decision_needed: Must export receipts enumerate each lost item per entry, or is per-class counting sufficient?

statement: Export record fields compatibility_notes (target-specific caveats for consumers) and warnings (anything that survived but degraded).
Export record fields source.lai (LAI the artifact was derived from) and result.digest (digest of the produced artifact).
decision_needed: Which digest algorithm(s) does result.digest use, and can several be recorded?

statement: Export record lacks fields present on import (tool and version, export mode such as --deterministic, normalisation rule-set version, source PCR/digest); without them deterministic re-export verification (§15.3) cannot be reproduced.
decision_needed: Should export receipts record tool version, export options and normalisation rule-set version?

statement: Where an export receipt lives is unspecified: a legacy artifact cannot embed a record containing its own result.digest; default location/naming without --receipt, and whether refused exports still emit a receipt, are unstated.
decision_needed: What is the default persistence of export receipts (sidecar file name, stdout, embedded in a sidecar .eb)?

statement: Provenance may be embedded and is by default: an imported archive carries its ConversionRecord in a CONVERSION_RECORD section.
The CONVERSION_RECORD section is covered by the AUX digest and therefore by any signature.
refines_or_supersedes: Depends on authoritative identity table SPEC §8.0 (L862)
research_needed: Test vectors showing AUX changes when CONVERSION_RECORD bytes change.

statement: No flag exists to opt out of embedding provenance at import time (only removal later via repack --strip-provenance); whether --receipt <file> replaces or duplicates the embedded record is unstated.
decision_needed: Should convert offer a no-embed option, and does --receipt write in addition to or instead of embedding?

statement: An embedded ConversionRecord exposes source digest, tool version, byte offsets and dropped data; whether it is encrypted in encrypted archives and what it reveals to non-recipients is not stated.
research_needed: Privacy analysis of CONVERSION_RECORD contents under encryption; confirm it falls under encrypted metadata rules.
decision_needed: Is CONVERSION_RECORD always inside the encryption envelope for encrypted archives?

statement: Under identity/v1 the ConversionRecord never participates in LAI; identical content with different provenance is logically the same archive, so re-importing a ZIP with a newer tool does not change the LAI of unchanged content.
research_needed: Test vector: same content imported with different tool versions/receipts yields identical LAI.

statement: A newer importer that resolves ambiguities or normalises metadata differently would change LAI regardless of provenance exclusion; how importer semantic changes are versioned and bound to identity is unaddressed.
research_needed: Track LAI stability of a legacy corpus across importer releases in CI.
decision_needed: Are import normalisation/resolution rules versioned so that LAI changes across tool versions are detectable and declared?

statement: Embedded provenance is structurally inert: no reader consults it to decide anything; it is a record, not a directive.
research_needed: Conformance/fuzz test that reader and extraction behaviour is independent of CONVERSION_RECORD contents.

statement: repack --strip-provenance removes the embedded ConversionRecord; LAI is unchanged, but AUX changes so any existing signature no longer verifies.
research_needed: Test: strip-provenance preserves LAI and changes AUX.

statement: repack --strip-provenance warns and refuses on signed archives unless --drop-signatures is given.
Trade-off accepted: provenance removal must invalidate signatures, because a provenance record that could be silently removed from a signed archive would be worthless.

Signatures appear to bind several roots separately (repack yields 'content VALID, physical STALE'), yet an AUX change makes 'any signature no longer verify'; which roots a signature binds and why AUX change is failure rather than a STALE binding is inconsistent.
research_needed: Formalise signature statement structure (LAI/PCR/AUX/PCI) and the verify status lattice; security review.
decision_needed: Does a signature bind AUX as a hard requirement or as a separately-reportable binding that can go STALE?

statement: Only import and export produce ConversionRecords; whether repack, key add/remove, or strip-provenance append a record to the provenance chain is unstated.
decision_needed: Do physical rewrites (repack, re-encrypt) add provenance records?

statement: A zip to eb to tar.zst pipeline produces an ordered provenance chain: the tarball receipt names the LAI it came from and the .eb embedded record names the source ZIP with its digest.
entrybound receipt --chain prints the whole derivation path.

How the chain is assembled across artifacts is unclear: receipt accepts only <archive.eb>, and it is unstated whether an export receipt copies upstream records or the user must supply each intermediate artifact.
decision_needed: Do export receipts embed the full upstream chain, and can receipt operate on a standalone receipt file or legacy artifact?

statement: Claims that asking what an artifact was derived from, by what tool, under what interpretation policy, and what was lost is currently unanswerable in every ecosystem.
research_needed: Survey SLSA/in-toto provenance, SPDX/CycloneDX pedigree, Sigstore attestations, Debian buildinfo to test 'every ecosystem'.

statement: Export and chain receipts are not stated to be signed or otherwise authenticated; derivation and describes_lai claims are unauthenticated assertions, and trust propagation along a chain is undefined.
research_needed: Threat model for forged receipts; evaluate signing receipts or wrapping in in-toto/DSSE attestations.
decision_needed: Can external receipts be signed, and what trust does receipt --chain assert?

statement: Simple operations are one line with no flags: 'entrybound pack ./project' produces project.eb using the balanced profile.
Advanced policy is discoverable, not memorised: every command's --help names applicable policy flags, and 'entrybound explain' reveals what was decided and why.
No command requires naming a codec, transform, dictionary or parameter; these are planner outputs visible on request.
refines_or_supersedes: Optional --dictionary <file> on pack (§17.3 L1845) is an allowed override, not a requirement

statement: CLI verbs describe outcomes, not mechanisms (e.g., verify answers 'is this sound', not 'recompute the CRC').
Dangerous things are named dangerous and are never defaults.
research_needed: Audit every CLI default against the dangerous-operation list.

statement: Output is human-readable by default and machine-readable on request via --format=json for every command producing structured output.

Synopses list --format only for list, diff and receipt (diff adds 'unified'); inspect, verify, explain, convert --dry-run and salvage --report omit it, and JSON schema stability/versioning is unspecified.
decision_needed: Is --format json mandatory on every structured-output command, and are JSON schemas versioned and stable?

statement: Process exit-code semantics are unspecified (e.g., verify with partial checks, STALE bindings, 'no signatures present', LOSSY dry-run), though scripts need machine-actionable status.
decision_needed: What exit-code taxonomy maps verify/convert/unpack outcomes, and is it tied to the named reason-code taxonomy?

statement: CLI has fourteen commands: pack, unpack, list, inspect, verify, convert, repack, diff, explain, receipt, sign, key, salvage, repair.
refines_or_supersedes: Chosen against the capability list in the design brief

statement: The fourteen-command set is claimed complete against the brief's capability list with no command duplicating another.
research_needed: Trace matrix from brief capabilities to commands; usability study of option complexity versus tar/7z/zip CLIs.

statement: The no-duplication claim is strained: unpack --verify-only overlaps verify --deep, and verify --against <dir|archive> overlaps diff against a directory or archive.
decision_needed: Should overlapping options be removed, or their distinct semantics (e.g., authoritative verdict vs report) documented?

statement: salvage and repair exist because §11.4 and §22.5 reference them normatively; a normative mechanism must not be delegated to a nonexistent command.
§11.4 cites salvage as specified in §17.4, but salvage is actually specified in §17.2; cross-reference is wrong.
decision_needed: Correct the §11.4 cross-reference to §17.2.

statement: salvage <archive.eb> [destination] supports --best-effort (recover what can be recovered from a damaged archive) and --report <file> (what was recovered and what was lost).
research_needed: Corruption-injection experiments measuring salvage recovery rate and blast radius.
decision_needed: What does salvage do without --best-effort, given the command is inherently best-effort?

statement: salvage is the only command that produces output from a non-conforming archive; this is what allows unpack to be strict.
refines_or_supersedes: Implements §11.4 L1386 strict parsing, no recovery mode
research_needed: Conformance test: unpack/list/verify reject all non-conforming corpus cases; only salvage emits output.

statement: Per I25, every salvage artifact is marked unverified in its report and, where the destination format allows, in-band; salvage never claims a signature verified.
The in-band 'unverified' marking mechanism for salvage outputs (e.g., directory destinations: xattr, filename suffix, marker file) is unspecified, as is what 'destination format allows' means.
research_needed: Platform feasibility of in-band markers (xattrs on Linux/macOS, ADS on Windows) and their survival on copy.
decision_needed: Which in-band marker is used per destination type?

statement: repair <archive.eb> --parity <file> [--out <file>] and verify <archive.eb> --parity <file> make an external parity artifact a first-class workflow.
research_needed: Select and test binding to a mature parity format (e.g., PAR2) including partial damage and parity-file damage.

statement: Parity is external by design; no in-archive error correction.
Which external parity format(s) are bound is not named here, and repair's behaviour when --out is omitted (in-place rewrite?) is unspecified.
decision_needed: Which parity format(s) are normative, and does repair without --out modify the archive in place atomically?

statement: A mount command is deferred to the ecosystem rather than the core CLI.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §19.5 L2156-2158 (mount is a filesystem with its own obligations)
research_needed: After random-access model is proven, prototype FUSE/WinFsp/macFUSE mount on the reader API.
decision_needed: When and by whom is a mount surface delivered post-v1?

statement: pack, unpack, list and verify are designated 'the core four' commands.
pack <input>... [output.eb] accepts --profile fast|balanced|dense|extreme with default balanced.
Default output naming for pack with multiple inputs, and default destination for unpack when [destination] is omitted, are unspecified.
decision_needed: What output path does pack derive for several inputs, and does unpack extract into CWD or a new directory named after the archive?

statement: pack --deterministic fixes the resource model to produce reproducible output.
research_needed: Reproducibility experiments across thread counts, memory, and machines.

statement: What 'fix the resource model' pins (threads, memory, planner time budget, planner version) is not stated; implies default pack output is not byte-reproducible.
research_needed: Measure compression-ratio and speed cost of deterministic mode versus default.
decision_needed: Should deterministic packing be the default, and what exact parameters does it pin?

statement: pack --recipient <spec> (repeatable) encrypts to recipients; --password encrypts with a prompted password.
Recipient <spec> syntax (key file path such as alice.pub, inline key string, identity URI) and non-interactive password input for scripts/CI are unspecified.
decision_needed: What recipient spec formats are accepted, and is non-interactive password input (fd/env) permitted?

statement: pack --sign <identity> signs the archive during creation.
pack --layout stream|indexed defaults to indexed, and to stream when output is a pipe.
pack --dictionary <file> supplies a dictionary instead of training one.
decision_needed: What dictionary file formats are accepted, and is the supplied dictionary embedded in the archive?

statement: pack --exclude <pattern>... excludes input paths.
decision_needed: Which pattern syntax (glob dialect, gitignore-style, regex) do --exclude, --include and --filter use, and is it consistent across commands?

statement: pack --metadata <class>... selects which metadata classes to capture.
decision_needed: What is the default captured class set and the CLI class names?

statement: pack --pad none|buckets|max controls encrypted-archive chunk padding, default buckets.
research_needed: Measure size overhead and leakage reduction of bucket vs max padding on realistic corpora.

statement: pack --chunk-boundary default|keyed-prf selects CDC boundary mode for encrypted archives; keyed-prf gives stronger boundaries at a cost.
keyed-prf chunk boundaries are described as 'provably-secure' at a cost; neither the proof nor the cost is given in this section.
research_needed: Formal security argument for keyed-PRF CDC against boundary/fingerprinting attacks; measure dedup and speed cost versus default.

statement: pack --dry-run plans and reports while writing nothing.
Enforced option exclusions are refused at parse time, each with its reason.
--password may not be combined with --recipient, because a cheap password undercuts every strong recipient.
A post-quantum recipient may not be combined with a classical-only recipient, since multi-recipient security is the minimum over its recipients.
Classifying a recipient as post-quantum or classical requires parsing key material, so 'refused at parse time' is ambiguous; also unaddressed whether key add later can introduce a mixed set.
decision_needed: Is the PQ/classical exclusion enforced at key-parse time and also on key add / repack --recipient?

statement: --recipient or --password combined with --layout stream is refused in v1.
Encrypted STREAM-layout archives are refused 'in v1', implying possible future support.
research_needed: Design of an online-authenticated encryption scheme for unknown-size streams (e.g., STREAM construction) compatible with the envelope.
decision_needed: Will encrypted stream layout be supported post-v1, and under what construction?

statement: Layout defaults to stream when output is a pipe, but encryption with stream layout is refused; behaviour of 'pack --recipient' writing to stdout (error, silent switch to indexed on non-seekable output, or buffering) is unspecified.
decision_needed: Does encrypted pack to a pipe fail with a named reason, or can indexed layout be written to non-seekable output?

statement: --pad and --chunk-boundary have no effect without encryption and are refused rather than silently ignored.
research_needed: Clarify that the default pad=buckets applies silently; refusal only when explicitly passed.

statement: unpack <archive.eb> [destination] accepts --policy <file|name> for extraction policy, default 'safe'.
decision_needed: What named policies exist and what is the policy file format?

statement: unpack --budget <spec> overrides resource limits.
decision_needed: What is the --budget spec syntax and which limits can be overridden?

statement: unpack supports --include / --exclude <pattern>... to select entries.
unpack --metadata <class>... selects which metadata classes to restore.
unpack --allow special-files,setuid,ownership,devices provides explicit opt-ins for dangerous restorations.

The --allow list names four categories; whether other dangerous restorations (symlinks escaping destination, hardlinks, security.* xattrs, NTFS ADS, quarantine-marker removal, sticky/setgid) need opt-ins is not stated here.
research_needed: Threat enumeration from historical extraction CVEs (tar/zip slip, symlink races, setuid) mapped to allow-categories.
decision_needed: Is the --allow category list closed, and which additional categories are required?

statement: unpack --on-collision refuse|rename|skip, default refuse.
decision_needed: Does 'collision' cover pre-existing destination files, intra-archive case/normalisation collisions on the destination filesystem, or both?

statement: unpack --identity <key> provides the decryption identity.
decision_needed: How are password-encrypted archives unpacked (automatic prompt?) given unpack lists no --password flag?

statement: unpack --verify-only decodes and verifies but writes nothing.
unpack has no --profile flag: a user never needs to know how an archive was made in order to read it.
refines_or_supersedes: SPEC §6.0 contract binding all four profiles (L647)
research_needed: Conformance: a single reader decodes archives from every profile without configuration.

statement: list <archive.eb> supports --long (kinds, sizes, modes, timestamps), --tree (hierarchical), --format json|text, and --filter <pattern>.
verify by default checks digests and structure; --deep decodes and verifies every chunk.

Which digests default verify can check without decoding chunks (stored-byte digests? Merkle over ciphertext?) and what default verify covers for an encrypted archive without a decryption identity are unspecified.
decision_needed: What exactly is verified by default for plaintext and encrypted archives with and without identity?

statement: verify --signatures verifies signatures and reports signers.
decision_needed: Where do trust roots/keyrings for signer acceptance come from, and does verify distinguish 'valid signature' from 'trusted signer'?

statement: verify --canonical checks canonical-form conformance.
verify --against <dir|archive> checks that content matches a directory or another archive.
verify --reproducible reports whether the archive is byte-reproducible and under what conditions.
How verify can determine byte-reproducibility from an archive alone is unexplained; it presumably needs recorded planner version and resource model, or a re-pack from source.
decision_needed: What metadata must an archive record for --reproducible to answer, and does it require source input?

statement: verify output is explicit about what was checked and what was not; a verify that did not decode chunk data says so.
research_needed: Conformance tests of verify output across every option combination.

statement: verify on an archive with no signatures reports 'no signatures present', never 'verified'.
inspect --fidelity reports what metadata was captured and what was not.
inspect --budgets reports declared resource requirements versus this machine's policy.
inspect --identity reports LAI, PCR, AUX, PCI and the identity profile in force.
inspect --features reports required, read-only-compatible, and optional features.
inspect --access reports random-access granularity and chunk-group lookback.
inspect --crypto reports suite, recipient count, commitment, and what is and is not hidden.
decision_needed: Is recipient count visible to non-recipients (a metadata leak), or only after decryption?

statement: inspect --layout reports stream or indexed layout, and index presence and size.
explain <archive.eb> [path] --entry <path> reports why an entry was stored the way it was.
explain --plan <id> reports the transform pipeline, codec, parameters and dictionary for a plan.
explain --savings reports where the bytes went, by category.
explain --rejected lists candidates the planner evaluated and rejected, with measured sizes.

explain runs on a finished archive, so rejected candidates, measured sizes and decision reasons must be stored in the archive or recomputed; storage location, identity-root coverage, size cost, determinism and leakage in encrypted archives are unaddressed.
research_needed: Measure planner decision-log size on large corpora; privacy analysis of per-entry candidate sizes.
decision_needed: Is the planner decision log embedded (which section, which digest root) or recomputed by re-planning?

statement: explain --verification reports which reconstructive transforms were verified and which fell back.
explain is claimed to make 'the user does not need to know the codec' acceptable rather than opaque, letting users see which candidates lost and by how much.
research_needed: Usability study with release engineers and archivists on explain output comprehension and trust.

statement: diff <a> <b> supports --logical (semantic model comparison, default), --physical (container bytes), --metadata (include non-identity metadata), and --format json|text|unified.
diff compares two archives, an archive against a directory, or an archive against a legacy artifact.
decision_needed: Under which import mode (strict, compat, preserve) is a legacy artifact interpreted for diff?

statement: Because LAI is defined, diff --logical on two archives of the same content packed with different profiles reports 'identical'.
research_needed: Property test: pack same tree under all four profiles, layouts and encryption; diff --logical reports identical.

statement: receipt <archive.eb> supports --chain (full derivation chain), --losses (only losses and warnings), and --format json|text.
One convert command handles both directions, inferred from file types; separate import/export verbs were rejected as primary, but import and export exist as first-class aliases.
How direction and type are 'inferred from the file types' is undefined (magic vs extension; destination may not exist), as are legacy-to-legacy or eb-to-eb requests and conflicts with --to.
decision_needed: Is direction inferred from source magic and destination extension, and what errors apply for ambiguous or same-kind pairs?

statement: convert --strict is the default for legacy to eb and refuses on ambiguity.
convert --compat <runtime> resolves ambiguities per a named legacy runtime.
decision_needed: What registry of runtime names (e.g., specific unzip/libarchive/Windows versions) is supported?

statement: convert --preserve retains non-semantic legacy peculiarities.
convert --to <format> gives the explicit target format for eb to legacy.
decision_needed: What format identifiers and dialect/target-profile names does --to accept?

statement: convert --accept-loss proceeds with a declared lossy export.
convert --deterministic produces byte-reproducible legacy output.
convert --dry-run reports the conversion plan and every ambiguity without writing.
convert --receipt <file> writes the receipt to a separate file.

convert (import) lists no profile, encryption, signing, layout or metadata-capture options; whether an imported archive can be encrypted/signed/profiled directly or requires a subsequent repack/sign is unstated.
decision_needed: Does convert accept pack-style options (--profile, --recipient, --sign) for legacy to eb?

statement: repack rewrites an archive with different physical parameters while preserving LAI; --profile re-plans with a different profile.
research_needed: Property test: repack across all profiles/layouts preserves LAI.

statement: repack supports --layout stream|indexed and --rebuild-index.
repack --strip-provenance removes provenance and invalidates signatures.
repack --add <path>... adds entries; this changes LAI, and the change is reported rather than implied.
repack is defined as LAI-preserving, yet --add changes LAI; and append is declared not offered (§24) while repack --add is effectively append-by-rewrite.
refines_or_supersedes: Tension with §24 non-goals (L2499) and repack purpose L1807
decision_needed: Should LAI-changing operations (--add) live under repack, and how is it distinguished from the refused append capability?

statement: repack --recipient / --identity re-encrypts to a new recipient set.
decision_needed: Does re-encryption change PCR/AUX and invalidate or stale signatures, and does it rotate the content key?

statement: repack --lookback <n> sets chunk-group lookback.
repack --chunk-boundary default|keyed-prf changes the CDC boundary mode.
repack --drop-signatures is required for any operation that invalidates signatures.
repack --verify-identity asserts LAI is unchanged; it is on by default, automatically off with --add, and is the guardrail that makes the identity model trustworthy in practice.
repack <archive.eb> [output.eb] with output omitted (as in the worked example) implies in-place rewrite; atomicity, crash safety and backup behaviour are unspecified.
decision_needed: Does repack without an output path rewrite in place via atomic replace, and what happens on interruption?

statement: sign <archive.eb> --identity <key> supports optional --detached <file> signatures and --timestamp <url> for a timestamp authority.
research_needed: Evaluate RFC 3161 TSA trust, availability and long-term validation for thirty-year archives.
decision_needed: Does an embedded signature modify the archive in place, and how is adding one signature kept from invalidating existing ones?

statement: sign is described as 'add or manage signatures' and key as 'manage recipients and identities', but only sign-add and key add/remove/list recipients are specified; signature listing/removal and identity/keypair generation are missing.
decision_needed: Which subcommands generate identities and list/remove signatures, or is key generation delegated to external tools?

statement: key add <archive.eb> --recipient <spec> adds a recipient to an archive.
decision_needed: Does key add require a decryption identity, only re-wrap the content key, and how does it affect signatures and AUX/PCR?

statement: key remove <archive.eb> --recipient <spec> performs a re-encrypt and says so.
research_needed: Measure re-encryption cost for large archives; confirm content key rotation.

statement: key list <archive.eb> lists recipients.
decision_needed: What recipient information can key list show without decrypting (recipient privacy)?

statement: key remove always prints a warning that re-encrypting revokes future access, but anyone who already read the archive can still decrypt any copy they hold.
Canonical verbs are pack and unpack: short, unambiguous, symmetric, and describing an archive operation rather than a codec operation.
refines_or_supersedes: Answers the design brief's alias question (compress/pack/create)

statement: Accepted aliases: create to pack, extract to unpack, c to pack, x to unpack, t to list; shown in --help as aliases for users arriving from tar and 7z.
research_needed: Usability check that tar-style single-letter aliases do not imply tar semantics (stdout output, flag bundling).

statement: compress/decompress aliases are rejected: they name the wrong operation and would invite expectation of a single-stream codec interface.
Entrybound does not provide a single-stream codec interface; users wanting to compress one stream should use a stream compressor.
Compression is one planner decision among several; an archive may legitimately contain no compressed bytes at all.
The alias 'a' for add is rejected as ambiguous with append.
Entrybound does not offer append.
Worked example (common case): 'pack ./project' then 'unpack project.eb' must work with no flags.
research_needed: Encode worked examples as CLI acceptance tests.

statement: Worked example (release engineering): pack dense deterministic signed; export zip deterministic; verify --deep --signatures.
research_needed: Encode as end-to-end acceptance test including byte-reproducibility checks.

statement: Worked example (encrypted multi-recipient): pack with --recipient alice.pub --recipient bob.pub, then inspect --crypto.
Worked example (auditing an untrusted ZIP before adoption): convert suspicious.zip out.eb --strict --dry-run, and verify suspicious.zip --canonical.
Worked example (understanding decisions): explain release.eb --entry lib/core.so and explain release.eb --savings.
Cheap re-optimisation: after repack to a different profile, the content signature survives while the physical binding goes stale; verify --signatures reports content VALID, physical STALE.
research_needed: Formal definition of signature statement over LAI and PCR; test repack across profiles produces VALID/STALE report.

statement: The signature status vocabulary (VALID, STALE, and presumably INVALID/untrusted) and the acceptance policy for a STALE physical binding in release verification are not defined here.
decision_needed: Is a STALE physical binding acceptable for consumers by default, and what is the full status vocabulary?

statement: One canonical extension, .eb, for every Entrybound archive regardless of encryption, layout, signing, native or converted origin, or sidecar role; the extension names the format, not its parameters.
The preamble states layout, features and encryption status in the first bytes, so the format is self-describing and needs no parameterised extensions.
research_needed: Confirm preamble spec and implementation expose layout, feature set and encryption status at fixed early offsets.

statement: Encryption status in the filename is a small metadata leak, free to avoid; note the preamble still exposes encryption status to anyone reading the first bytes.
research_needed: Privacy analysis of what an observer learns from preamble versus filename.

statement: One extension means one handler, MIME type, magic entry, PRONOM signature, shell completion and file-manager association; each extra extension multiplies these.
Container formats that proliferated extensions (.tar.gz, .tgz, .tar.zst, etc.) did so because the container could not describe its own compression.
research_needed: Historical check of extension proliferation causes (tar + external compressor pipelines, DOS 8.3 names).

statement: The .eb extension collides with at least one existing HPC tool's plain-text configuration files; the collision is claimed low-impact because the files are text and the ecosystems do not overlap.
research_needed: Survey .eb usage (e.g., EasyBuild easyconfigs), existing shared-mime-info/libmagic/Windows associations; assess HPC and research-data archive user overlap.

statement: Claims every modern identification path (libmagic, freedesktop shared-mime-info) resolves by magic number ahead of glob.
research_needed: Check shared-mime-info spec checking order (glob weights vs magic priority), Windows Explorer and macOS UTI (extension-based), browsers and web servers mapping by extension.

statement: Extension choice is not final: if the implementation team prefers zero collision risk, .eba is the fallback, with nothing else in the specification changing.
research_needed: Collision survey for both .eb and .eba across registries, OS associations and common tools.
decision_needed: Is the canonical extension .eb or .eba?

statement: Rejected extensions: .ebz (implies a specific codec), .ebx (suggests experimental), and any encrypted-specific variant.
Media type is application/vnd.entrybound.archive, registered in the vendor tree under RFC 6838.
Claims the standards tree is effectively closed to a new project and recent archive-adjacent registrations use the vendor tree, adding a structured-syntax suffix when built on an existing container.
research_needed: Survey IANA media-type registry for recent archive/container registrations and suffix usage.

statement: The media type takes no structured-syntax suffix because Entrybound is not built on another container.
Registration step 1: preliminary community review by posting the template to the media-types review list.
Registration step 2: submit the RFC 6838 template with complete Security considerations citing §11 and a Published specification field pointing at a stable, archived, versioned specification URL.
research_needed: Establish a stable, archived, versioned public specification URL (prerequisite).
decision_needed: Where and when is a stable versioned public specification published to satisfy the template?

statement: Registration step 3: declare Magic number(s) and File extension(s) in the template's additional-information block, since downstream identification tooling consumes them.
refines_or_supersedes: Depends on magic freeze (§18.3 L2073) and extension choice (§18.1 L2036)

statement: Registration intended usage COMMON; change controller is the Entrybound project.
decision_needed: What legal/organisational entity is 'the Entrybound project' for change control?

statement: If a standards body later adopts Entrybound, application/entrybound in the standards tree becomes available and the vendor type remains valid as a deprecated alias.
decision_needed: Would Entrybound pursue standards-body adoption, and when?

statement: The magic number is eight bytes at offset 0, following the PNG signature rationale, plus two archive-specific additions.
Magic byte 1 is at least 0x80, so the file is never valid ASCII, unlikely valid UTF-8, and high-bit-clearing transfers are detected.
Magic bytes 2-4 are 'E', 'B' and a generation digit, readable in head and strings.

The semantics of the generation digit are unspecified: when it increments relative to format version, feature bits and identity profiles, and whether changing it breaks existing readers and registry signatures.
decision_needed: What event bumps the generation digit, and do registry entries match all generations?

statement: Magic bytes 5-6 are CR LF (detect newline translation), byte 7 is 0x1A (stops naive text display), byte 8 is LF (detects inverse newline translation).
The concrete proposed magic is 8E 45 42 31 0D 0A 1A 0A (0x8E, E, B, 1, CR, LF, SUB, LF).
refines_or_supersedes: Subject to freeze-time verification in §18.3 L2073
research_needed: Check whether the implementation already hard-codes this value before the database-collision verification.

statement: Archive-specific addition 1: a trailer magic plus declared total length (§4.4) lets a reader decide exactly and cheaply: complete, truncated at N bytes, or corrupt.
research_needed: Check whether 'cheap' holds for STREAM layout on non-seekable input, and for unknown-size streams where total length cannot be declared up front.

statement: Truncation is claimed to be the dominant real-world failure for archives, which a leading magic alone cannot detect.
research_needed: Empirical data on archive failure modes (interrupted downloads, disk-full, bit rot, transfer mangling) from bug trackers or storage studies.

statement: Archive-specific addition 2: a feature-bitmap checksum (§4.2) lets a reader distinguish 'corrupt' from 'uses a feature I do not implement'.
Claims that distinguishing corrupt from unimplemented features is a refinement one stream format has and no archive format does.
research_needed: Survey header checksums and feature flags in xz, zstd, 7z, RAR5, ZIP, squashfs, WIM.

statement: The chosen magic sequence must be neither a prefix of, nor prefixed by, any entry in the standard identification databases; this is verified before the value is frozen.
research_needed: Check libmagic Magdir, shared-mime-info, PRONOM/DROID, Apache Tika, TrID for prefix conflicts with 8E 45 42 31 0D 0A 1A 0A; define how short (1-2 byte) entries are treated.

statement: The magic value is not yet frozen: database-collision verification is a stated precondition that has not been reported as done.
research_needed: Perform and record the identification-database prefix verification.
decision_needed: Freeze 8E 45 42 31 0D 0A 1A 0A as the magic after verification, or choose another value?

statement: Three identification registrations are necessary: IANA media type, libmagic/file(1), and freedesktop shared-mime-info; IANA gives the canonical name that the others treat as legitimacy evidence.
decision_needed: Are these registrations release gates for v1 or post-release tasks?

statement: libmagic/file(1) registration: a magic entry with !:mime and !:ext directives and an explicit strength adjustment so it ranks correctly against glob collisions.
research_needed: Confirm libmagic ranking semantics: strength orders magic entries among themselves; file(1) does not glob-match, so 'against glob collision' may be a misstatement.

statement: freedesktop shared-mime-info registration: an XML package with a glob and a prioritised magic match.
research_needed: Choose magic priority and glob weight so .eb files are identified correctly despite existing .eb glob uses.

statement: A PRONOM signature must also be registered, as a separate act from IANA, so digital-preservation identification tooling can name .eb files.

Claims that without PRONOM preservation repositories cannot name an .eb file at all, and that archives and libraries most care about a thirty-year format yet are least likely to be reached by a GitHub release.
research_needed: Interview/survey preservation practitioners (DROID/Siegfried users) on identification workflows and adoption channels.
